title: The Mill Fire
subtitle: A chronology and causation warm-up
summary: Seven undated papers about a mill that burned. Students put them in the order they were written, using only what each one takes for granted, then decide how much the sequence lets them say about why it burned.
social_topology: Individual copies, or pairs on one device
sources_rights: No real sources are used. Every document is invented for the exercise.

human_tests.note: Opened as a file:// URL and played to the ending; the page loaded no resources beyond itself.
Rounds one and three were played with Tab and Enter only. Every control was reachable, focus stayed on the moved card's button after each move, and a visible outline showed at each step.
Estimated at 5-8 minutes from an 870-word path plus the ordering moves, not timed with a player.
No classroom setup to test against. The instructor must do this.
There are no real sources to check against. The game states this on its Sources & assumptions screen.
Five debrief questions ship on the ending screen.

provenance_note: This game uses no historical sources at all. Every paper in it is invented to carry two specific problems: dating undated documents from their internal cross-references, and separating the date a document was written from the date of what it describes. It is a method exercise, not a history lesson.
